Histology.question: ১) The trochanters of the femur are....... epiphysis?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is traction epiphysis. The trochanters of the femur are examples of traction epiphyses because they develop at sites where muscles and tendons attach and exert pulling forces.

  • Pressure epiphysis – Develops at joint surfaces and transmits pressure (e.g., head of femur).

  • Atavistic epiphysis – Represents a bone that was independent in evolution but became fused (e.g., coracoid process).

  • Aberrant epiphysis – An unusual or accessory epiphysis.

High-yield points:

  • Traction epiphysis → Muscle pull → Greater & lesser trochanters

  • Pressure epiphysis → Articular surface → Head of femur

  • Epiphysis → End part of long bone

Histology.question: ২) Which Epithelial cell junction is devoid of any Cytoskeletal components?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is gap junction. Gap junctions are intercellular communication channels formed by connexons and do not have direct attachment to cytoskeletal elements.

  • Tight junction – Associated with actin cytoskeleton through ZO proteins.

  • Adherens junction – Linked to actin filaments.

  • Desmosome – Anchored to intermediate filaments.

High-yield points:

  • Tight junction → Actin

  • Adherens junction → Actin

  • Desmosome → Intermediate filament

  • Gap junction → Cell communication via connexins

Histology.question: ৩) What is the type of sweat gland according to structural classification of exocrine gland?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is simple coiled tubular gland. Sweat glands are simple tubular exocrine glands with a coiled secretory portion.

  • Simple tubular – Straight tubular glands.

  • Compound tubular – Branched duct system.

  • Compound tubuloacinar – Mixed gland structure.

High-yield points:

  • Sweat gland → Simple coiled tubular

  • Sebaceous gland → Simple branched acinar

  • Salivary gland → Compound tubuloacinar

Histology.question: ৪) Which is not criteria of skeletal muscle?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is centrally placed nucleus. Skeletal muscle fibres are multinucleated with peripheral nuclei, not central nuclei.

  • Single multinucleated cells – True (long multinucleated fibres).

  • Cylindrical shape – True.

  • Voluntary movements – True.

High-yield points:

  • Skeletal muscle → Multinucleated + peripheral nuclei + striated + voluntary

  • Cardiac muscle → Single central nucleus

Histology.question: ৫) What is the lining epithelium of Conjunctiva?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is stratified columnar epithelium. The conjunctiva is lined mainly by stratified columnar epithelium with goblet cells.

  • Simple columnar – Found in intestine.

  • Simple cuboidal – Kidney tubules.

  • Stratified cuboidal – Large ducts.

High-yield points:

  • Conjunctiva → Stratified columnar + goblet cells

  • Cornea → Stratified squamous non-keratinized

Histology.question: ৬) Which of the following serves to cushion and insulate the skin and other organs?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is adipocyte. Adipocytes store fat and provide energy storage, thermal insulation, and mechanical cushioning.

  • Histiocytes/macrophages – Immune functions.

  • Fibroblasts – Produce connective tissue fibres.

High-yield points:

  • Adipose tissue → Cushion + insulation + energy storage

Histology.question: ৭) Functions of the basement membrane include which of the following?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is molecular filtering. Basement membrane acts as a selective barrier controlling movement of molecules between epithelium and connective tissue.

  • Contractility – Muscle function.

  • Active ion transport – Specialized epithelial cells.

  • Excitability – Nerve and muscle property.

High-yield points:

  • Basement membrane → Support + filtration + cell adhesion

Histology.question: ৮) Which is the key cells in connective tissue proper?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is fibroblast. Fibroblasts are the main cells of connective tissue proper and produce collagen, elastin, and extracellular matrix.

  • Adipocytes – Fat storage.

  • Plasma cells – Antibody production.

  • Macrophages – Phagocytosis.

High-yield points:

  • Fibroblast → Main CT cell → Collagen production

Histology.question: ৯) Reticular connective tissue is absent in.....?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is thymus. Reticular connective tissue is a specialized type of connective tissue mainly composed of reticular fibres (type III collagen) and reticular cells. It forms a supportive meshwork (stroma) in several organs.

  • Bone marrow – Contains abundant reticular connective tissue, which forms the framework supporting hematopoietic cells.

  • Liver – Contains reticular fibres that support hepatocytes and form the structural framework around sinusoids.

  • Pancreas – Contains reticular fibres within its connective tissue framework.

  • Thymus – Does not contain reticular connective tissue. The supporting framework is formed by epithelial reticular cells, which are derived from endoderm and are different from reticular connective tissue.

High-yield points:

  • Reticular connective tissue → Type III collagen

  • Main locations → Bone marrow, lymph nodes, spleen, liver

  • Thymus → Epithelial reticular cells (not reticular connective tissue)

  • Common MCQ trap → “Reticular” in thymus does not mean reticular connective tissue

Histology.question: ১০) Which is not criteria of smooth muscle?
Histology.option1: Single small, closely packed fusiform cells
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is T tubules present. Smooth muscle lacks T tubules; instead, it has caveolae.

  • Fusiform cells – True.

  • No striations – True.

  • Involuntary movement – True.

High-yield points:

  • Smooth muscle → No striation + no T tubules + involuntary

Histology.question: ১১) What is the lining epithelium of thyroid?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is simple cuboidal epithelium. The thyroid gland is composed of thyroid follicles, which are lined by a single layer of cuboidal follicular cells. These cells synthesize and secrete thyroid hormones (T3 and T4).

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Stratified cuboidal epithelium – Found in larger ducts of glands, such as sweat glands, but not thyroid follicles.

  • Simple columnar epithelium – Seen in organs involved in absorption and secretion, such as intestine.

  • Stratified columnar epithelium – Rare; found in parts of male reproductive tract and large ducts.

High-yield points:

  • Thyroid follicle → Simple cuboidal epithelium

  • Thyroid follicles contain colloid → storage of thyroglobulin

  • Parathyroid → chief cells + oxyphil cells

Histology.question: ১২) Shaft of the long bones are formed from....?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is diaphysis. The shaft of a long bone is called the diaphysis, which develops mainly from the primary ossification centre.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Epiphysis – Forms the ends of long bones and develops from secondary ossification centres.

  • Metaphysis – The region between diaphysis and epiphysis containing the growth plate in growing bones.

  • Epiphyseal plate of cartilage – Responsible for longitudinal growth but is not the shaft.

High-yield points:

  • Diaphysis → Shaft → Primary ossification centre

  • Epiphysis → Bone ends → Secondary ossification centre

  • Epiphyseal plate → Longitudinal bone growth

Histology.question: ১৩) Which of the following is not dense regular connective tissue?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is dermis of skin. Dense regular connective tissue contains parallel collagen fibres arranged in the same direction to resist tensile forces.

The other options are examples of dense regular connective tissue:

  • Ligaments – Connect bone to bone; collagen fibres arranged regularly.

  • Tendons – Connect muscle to bone; highly organized collagen bundles.

  • Aponeuroses – Flat sheets of dense regular connective tissue connecting muscles.

The dermis of skin is mainly dense irregular connective tissue, where collagen fibres are arranged randomly to withstand stress from multiple directions.

High-yield points:

  • Dense regular CT → Tendon, ligament, aponeurosis

  • Dense irregular CT → Dermis, organ capsules

  • Regular = parallel collagen arrangement

Histology.question: ১৪) Which of the following is network or sheet-forming collagen?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is collagen type IV. Type IV collagen forms a network or sheet-like structure and is the main collagen component of the basement membrane.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Type I collagen – Most abundant collagen; found in bone, tendon, ligament, and skin.

  • Type II collagen – Found mainly in cartilage and vitreous humour.

  • Type III collagen – Forms reticular fibres supporting organs such as lymph nodes and bone marrow.

High-yield points:

  • Type I → Bone, tendon, ligament

  • Type II → Cartilage

  • Type III → Reticular fibres

  • Type IV → Basement membrane

Histology.question: ১৫) What is the lining epithelium of vagina?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is non-keratinised stratified squamous epithelium. The vaginal mucosa requires protection against friction while maintaining a moist surface, so it is lined by multiple layers of squamous cells without keratin.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Simple squamous epithelium – Found in areas requiring diffusion, such as alveoli and endothelium.

  • Keratinised stratified squamous epithelium – Found in skin, providing protection against abrasion and water loss.

  • Transitional epithelium – Found in urinary tract, especially bladder.

High-yield points:

  • Vagina → Non-keratinised stratified squamous

  • Skin → Keratinised stratified squamous

  • Urinary bladder → Transitional epithelium

Histology.question: ১৬) Which cartilage has no perichondrium?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is fibrocartilage. Fibrocartilage lacks a perichondrium because it is designed to withstand strong tensile and compressive forces and blends directly with surrounding dense connective tissue.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Hyaline cartilage – Usually has perichondrium except at articular surfaces.

  • Elastic cartilage – Has perichondrium and contains abundant elastic fibres.

  • All of them have perichondrium – Incorrect because fibrocartilage is the exception.

High-yield points:

  • Fibrocartilage → No perichondrium

  • Hyaline cartilage → Perichondrium present (except articular cartilage)

  • Elastic cartilage → Perichondrium present

Histology.question: ১৭) Which is not criteria of cardiac muscle?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is striations absent. Cardiac muscle is a striated muscle because it contains organized actin and myosin filaments arranged into sarcomeres. Therefore, absence of striations is not a feature of cardiac muscle.

The other options are true features of cardiac muscle:

  • Aligned cells in branching arrangement – Cardiac muscle fibres are short, cylindrical, and arranged in a branching network connected by intercalated discs.

  • Cylindrical in shape – Cardiac muscle cells are cylindrical and elongated.

  • Central nucleus – Cardiac myocytes usually contain a single centrally located nucleus.

High-yield points:

  • Cardiac muscle → Striated + involuntary + branching fibres + central nucleus

  • Skeletal muscle → Striated + voluntary + multiple peripheral nuclei

  • Smooth muscle → Non-striated + spindle-shaped + single central nucleus

Histology.question: ১৮) What is the content of lacunae?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is osteocyte. In mature bone, osteocytes are the mature bone cells located within small spaces called lacunae. They maintain the bone matrix and communicate through canaliculi.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Osteoprogenitor cells – Stem cells that give rise to osteoblasts; found in periosteum and endosteum.

  • Osteoblasts – Bone-forming cells located on bone surfaces; they synthesize osteoid.

  • Osteoclasts – Large multinucleated cells responsible for bone resorption.

High-yield points:

  • Lacunae → Osteocytes

  • Osteoblast → Bone formation

  • Osteoclast → Bone resorption

  • Canaliculi → Communication between osteocytes

Histology.question: ১৯) Which is not a location of elastic cartilage?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is eyelids. Elastic cartilage provides flexibility and support and is found in structures that require bending without losing shape. Eyelids do not contain elastic cartilage.

The other options are locations of elastic cartilage:

  • External ear (pinna) – Provides flexible support while maintaining shape.

  • Epiglottis – Allows flexible closure of the laryngeal inlet during swallowing.

  • Eustachian tube – Contains elastic cartilage supporting the auditory tube.

High-yield points:

  • Elastic cartilage → External ear, epiglottis, auditory tube

  • Hyaline cartilage → Trachea, nose, articular surfaces

  • Fibrocartilage → Intervertebral disc, pubic symphysis, meniscus

Histology.question: ২০) What is the lining epithelium of nasal cavity?
Histology.exp:
The correct answer is pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium. The respiratory part of the nasal cavity is lined by respiratory epithelium, which contains ciliated columnar cells, goblet cells, and basal cells.

The given option "pseudostratified squamous" is not the correct histological term; the correct term is pseudostratified columnar epithelium. Among the options, খ is the intended answer.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Simple squamous epithelium – Found in alveoli and blood vessels, where diffusion is needed.

  • Stratified squamous epithelium – Found in areas exposed to abrasion, such as the oral cavity and skin.

  • Transitional epithelium – Found in urinary tract.

High-yield points:

  • Nasal cavity respiratory mucosa → Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium + goblet cells

  • Goblet cells → Mucus secretion

  • Cilia → Mucociliary clearance
